mainTopic: Does nullified impurity still 'count'? The amud tests revival (ניעור) and impurity by carrying through mixtures of פרה אדומה ashes, נבילה, and a blood clot.
overview: The amud continues a proof that a nullified item can 'wake up' (ניעור) when it meets more of its own kind. According to רבי אליעזר, a nullified mixture must be eaten dry, roasted, kneaded with fruit juice, or in small batches. עולא explains that this is a decree, because a trace of impurity in the mixture could revive new impure food that someone adds. אביי answers that this only shows impurity reviving impurity, not purity reviving impurity. He then challenges the idea that nullified impurity still counts, using פרה אדומה ashes mixed with ordinary ashes. The reply is that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא ruled that such a mixture does not make one impure by touching but does make one impure by carrying. אביי pushes back with רב חסדא's ruling that a נבילה is nullified in slaughtered meat. רב דימי replies that his tradition follows רבי חייא, which gives the same touching/carrying split. Then אביי cites רבי חייא's teaching that a blood clot (חררת דם) makes no impurity even by carrying, and רב דימי is silent. The גמרא suggests he could have answered that the clot is decayed impurity. This works for בר פדא, and the גמרא begins to ask about רבי יוחנן's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How to eat a nullified mixture according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אליעזר, the nullified mixture may be eaten, but only in ways that keep it from becoming susceptible to טומאה or from having a full כביצה in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, what should be done with this food? It should be eaten dry or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into small doughs, as long as there is never an egg's volume in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a source about a mixture in which impure תרומה was nullified. It lists the special ways the leftover food must be eaten, and this source is being used as evidence in the larger discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food only becomes able to receive טומאה after water or similar liquids touch it, which is called הכשר. Fruit juice does not do this, so 'dry,' 'roasted,' and 'fruit juice' all keep the food from becoming susceptible. Food smaller than a כביצה cannot pass on food-impurity, so small batches are also safe. The question is why any of this is needed if the impurity was already nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry, crumbly baked goods, made without water
Roasted kernels
Fruit juice, which does not make food susceptible to טומאה
Doughs or batches
An egg's volume, the minimum size for food to transmit טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the food is still forbidden. It is permitted to eat. The restrictions are only about HOW it is eaten, so the tiny bit of nullified impurity never gets a chance to 'wake up.'

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, what will be with them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to the food left in the mixture after the nullification.

phrases.english: Let them be eaten dry, or roasted,
phrases.notes: No water touches the food, so it never becomes susceptible to impurity.

phrases.english: or let them be kneaded with fruit juice,
phrases.notes: Fruit juice does not make food susceptible to impurity.

phrases.english: or let it be divided into small doughs,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כְּבֵיצָה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: provided there is not an egg-bulk in one place.
phrases.notes: Less than a כביצה cannot transmit food-impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof begun on the previous amud that a nullified item can be revived.
steps.raayaObject: That a nullified item can 'wake up' when it meets its own kind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling according to רבי אליעזר that the nullified mixture must be eaten dry, roasted, with fruit juice, or in small batches.

steps.title: עולא explains the reason: the nullified impurity can wake up
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the restriction is a גזירה. A person might add impure produce and rely on a majority to nullify it, but the trace of impurity already in the mixture would revive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: What is the reason? It is a decree, in case someone brings a קב of impure חולין from somewhere else and a קב and a bit more from this mixture. He thinks, 'I will nullify the impure food with the majority.' But since there is a tiny amount of impurity already here, the kind finds its own kind and wakes up.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains why the food must be kept dry. The concern is that the small bit of nullified impurity could later 'wake up' new impurity that is added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an impure קב mixed with slightly more than a קב of pure food is nullified by majority. Here, though, the mixture already contains a trace of impurity. That trace joins the new impure food and tips it out of nullification. This is the core of the proof: a nullified item is treated as still present enough to 'reawaken.'

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic protective decree
A קב and a bit more, which is just enough to form a majority
Nullification by majority
A tiny trace amount
Wakes up, meaning a nullified item becomes active again

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the idea of מין במינו ניעור, that like meeting like can undo a nullification. The rest of this passage tests how far that idea goes.

phrases.english: And Ulla said: What is the reason?
It is a decree, lest one bring
a kav of impure non-sacred produce from another place
and a kav and a bit more from this kind (the mixture),
thinking: I will nullify them with the majority,
but since there is this tiny amount of impurity in the mixture,
the kind finds its own kind and wakes up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1, which turns it into evidence for revival.
steps.raayaObject: A nullified item can be revived when it meets its own kind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's explanation of רבי אליעזר's restrictions.

steps.title: אביי: impurity waking impurity is not the same as purity waking impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. In עולא's case, the thing that wakes the impurity is itself impure. That does not show that something pure can wake impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even if impurity wakes up impurity, does purity wake up impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רב דימי that the proof from steps 1–2 does not fit the case being discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עולא's case, the trace of impurity in the mixture wakes up the new impure food, so it is impurity reviving impurity. In the case under discussion, the thing that would do the 'waking' is pure. So the proof only covers a narrower situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Awakens or revives
Ritual impurity
Ritual purity

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם טוּמְאָה עוֹרֶרֶת טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: If impurity awakens impurity,
does purity awaken impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִם טוּמְאָה עוֹרֶרֶת טוּמְאָה טׇהֳרָה עוֹרֶרֶת טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn from עולא's explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison to the current case, not עולא's reasoning itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the source, the reviving agent is impure. In the case being discussed, the reviving agent is pure.

steps.title: Challenge from red heifer ashes mixed with ordinary ashes
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that when פרה אדומה ashes mix with ordinary ashes, we follow the majority. If the majority is ordinary ash, the mixture does not make one impure. But if nullified impurity still counts as present, carrying the mixture should still make a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: Fit ashes that mixed with ordinary burnt ashes follow the majority regarding impurity. If most is ordinary ash, it does not make impure. But if you say impurity is considered as if it is still there, then fine, it does not make impure by touching. It should still make impure by carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a משנה to attack the idea that nullified impurity is treated as still present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you touch a mixture, you may only be touching the ordinary ash, so it makes sense that touching does not make you impure. When you carry the whole mixture, though, you are certainly lifting the heifer ash along with it. If nullified impurity still 'exists,' carrying should make you impure. Yet the משנה seems to say the mixture is simply not impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid ashes of the פרה אדומה
Ordinary burnt ashes
We follow the majority
Impurity transmitted by touching
Impurity transmitted by carrying

steps.confusionAlert: Touching and carrying are two different ways impurity spreads. With touching, you might have touched only the ordinary ash. With carrying, you lift everything. That difference is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.english: He raised an objection: Fit (red heifer) ashes
that became mixed with ordinary burnt ashes,
we follow the majority regarding imparting impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי רוּבָּא אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה הוּא — לָא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.english: and if the majority is ordinary ash, it does not impart impurity.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ: טוּמְאָה כְּמַאן דְּאִיתֵיהּ דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: And if you say impurity is considered as though it is present,
granted that it does not impart impurity through touching,
let it impart impurity through carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof, אביי now actively challenges the idea that nullified impurity still counts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that nullified impurity is treated as still present (כמאן דאיתיה דמי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the heifer ash is still considered present, carrying the mixture lifts it, so the mixture should make one impure by carrying. The משנה implies it does not impart impurity at all.

steps.title: Answer: the mixture does make one impure by carrying
steps.stepSummary: The answer quotes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who already explained the משנה. The mixture does not make one impure by touching, but it does make one impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was already stated about this: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It is pure in that it does not make impure by touching, but it does make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by showing that an אמורא already read the משנה exactly the way the challenger said it 'should' be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'does not impart impurity' refers only to touching. For carrying, the heifer ash is still counted, so a person who carries the mixture becomes impure. This actually supports the idea that nullified impurity is considered present.

keyTerms.meaning: It was already stated about this (the source)
Pure in the sense of not making others impure

steps.whatToRemember: Ashes of the פרה אדומה nullified in ordinary ash do not make one impure by touching, but they still make one impure by carrying. A nullified impurity can still 'count' in some ways.

phrases.english: It was already stated about it:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
It is pure regarding imparting impurity through touching,
but it imparts impurity through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge from the red heifer ashes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source's ruling to one mode of impurity (touching only).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the mixture imparts no impurity at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixture is pure only regarding touching. It still imparts impurity through carrying, consistent with nullified impurity being considered present.

steps.title: אביי challenges from רב חסדא's ruling on a carcass mixed with slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רב חסדא, who says a נבילה is nullified in slaughtered meat. If nullified impurity still counted, it should at least make one impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חסדא say: a carcass is nullified in slaughtered meat, because a carcass can never become slaughtered meat? Fine, it does not make impure by touching. But it should make impure by carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the idea that nullified impurity still makes one impure by carrying. He brings a ruling of רב חסדא that treats the carcass as simply nullified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says a minority of נבילה is nullified in a majority of kosher slaughtered meat. He gives no hint that some impurity remains. אביי argues that if the hidden carcass still 'counts,' the mixture should at least make one impure by carrying, and רב חסדא's ruling does not suggest that.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it makes things impure
Meat from a properly slaughtered animal; it is pure
Nullified; lost in the majority
Touching, one way impurity is passed on
Carrying, a stricter way impurity is passed on (even without touching)

steps.confusionAlert: Touching (מגע) and carrying (משא) are two different ways to become impure. A נבילה makes a person impure in both ways. The whole debate is whether nullification removes both, or only the impurity from touching.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
a carcass is nullified in slaughtered meat,
since it is impossible for a carcass
to become slaughtered meat.
Granted that it does not make impure by touching,
let it make impure by carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5, which said the mixture still makes one impure by carrying.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a nullified mixture still makes one impure by carrying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא treats the carcass as fully nullified. That clashes with the idea that impurity by carrying remains.

steps.title: רב דימי answers that his tradition follows רבי חייא, not רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says: you follow רב חסדא, but we follow רבי חייא. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explained רבי חייא's teaching to mean that the mixture does not make impure by touching, but does make impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learn it like רב חסדא; we learn it like רבי חייא. רבי חייא taught: a carcass and slaughtered meat nullify each other. On this, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: it is pure in that it does not make impure by touching, but it does make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי does not defend רב חסדא. He says his side holds a different tradition, from רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that two traditions disagree. According to רבי חייא, as explained by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, nullification removes only the impurity from touching. Impurity by carrying remains, so רב חסדא's ruling is no problem for רב דימי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn it / our tradition teaches it
They nullify one another, depending on which is the majority
It was said about it (a later אמורא explaining an earlier teaching)

phrases.english: He (Rav Dimi) said to him:
You learn it according to Rav Chisda,
we learn it according to Rabbi Chiyya.
Rabbi Chiyya taught:
a carcass and slaughtered meat nullify one another,
and it was said about it,
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
it is pure in that it does not make impure by touching,
but it does make impure by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן בִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן בִּדְרַבִּי חִיָּיא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing tradition: the challenger's source follows a different tradition than the defender's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's full nullification would be binding on everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי חייא, as explained by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, nullification removes impurity by touching but not impurity by carrying.

steps.title: אביי challenges from the blood clot, and רב דימי is silent
steps.stepSummary: An animal that expelled a blood clot (חררת דם) is exempt from בכורה, and רבי חייא teaches that the clot makes no impurity at all, not by touching and not by carrying. Why not by carrying? רב דימי has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what we learned: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a large animal that expelled a clot of blood must have it buried, and the animal is exempt from בכורה. And רבי חייא taught: it does not make impure, not by touching and not by carrying. Why? Fine, it does not make impure by touching, but it should make impure by carrying! He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second challenge, this time from a case in our משנה. רב דימי cannot answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clot may contain a fetus. That fetus would be a נבילה, but it is lost inside the blood. According to רב דימי, such hidden impurity should still make one impure by carrying, yet רבי חייא himself says it makes no impurity at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A clot or mass of congealed blood expelled from the womb
It must be buried, out of concern that it may be a firstborn
Exempt from firstborn status; the next offspring is not a בכור
He was silent; he had no answer

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge uses רבי חייא, the very source רב דימי just relied on. That is why the question hits so hard.

phrases.english: And that which we learned (in the Mishnah):
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
a large animal that expelled a clot of blood
this (clot) must be buried,
and the animal is exempt from firstborn status.
And Rabbi Chiyya taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: it does not make impure, not by touching and not by carrying.
Why?
Granted that it does not make impure by touching,
let it make impure by carrying!
He (Rav Dimi) was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 answered the רב חסדא challenge, אביי brings a new challenge from רבי חייא himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's view that nullified impurity still makes impure by carrying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא rules that the clot makes no impurity by carrying, even though, according to רב דימי, the hidden fetus should.

steps.title: The גמרא suggests an answer: the clot is decayed impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why רב דימי was silent. He could have said the clot is different because it is decayed impurity (טומאה סרוחה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps here is surely different, because it is decayed impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an answer רב דימי could have given. The blood clot case is special because the impurity has rotted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity that has decayed loses its power to make things impure. So the clot makes no impurity for that reason, not because nullification removes impurity by carrying. If this works, רב דימי's view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Decayed or rotted impurity, which no longer makes things impure
Here is different (a special case)

phrases.english: Perhaps, surely here is different,
since it is decayed impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רב דימי was silent in step 8 and proposes a defense for him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the clot's impurity is decayed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clot shows that nullified impurity does not make impure by carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clot is pure only because its impurity has rotted, so it proves nothing about nullification.

steps.title: The decay answer fits בר פדא, but what about רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The decay answer works for בר פדא. He holds that severe impurity lasts only until the item is unfit for a גר, and a clot is unfit for a גר. The גמרא begins asking how it works for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for בר פדא, who said: severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a גר, and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog. This clot is not fit for a גר. But according to רבי יוחנן, who says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the decay answer works for everyone. It shows that it fits בר פדא, then begins a challenge from רבי יוחנן's view, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בר פדא, severe impurity (like נבילה, which makes impure by carrying) stops once the item is too spoiled for a גר תושב to eat. A blood clot is not fit for a גר, so its severe impurity is gone. רבי יוחנן apparently holds a different standard, so the answer may not work for him.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (according to a certain opinion)
Severe impurity, which makes impure even by carrying
Light impurity, which makes impure only by touching
Here, a גר תושב, who may eat נבילה

steps.confusionAlert: Here גר does not mean a convert. It means a גר תושב, a non-Jew who may eat נבילה. The test is whether the food is still fit for him.

phrases.english: This works well for Bar Padda, who said:
severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a ger,
and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog,
and this (clot) is not fit for a ger.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who says:
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the decay answer of step 9 against different opinions on when impurity ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decay answer offered in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on בר פדא's standard. רבי יוחנן's standard, quoted on the next amud, may keep the clot impure.
